expected_behaviors: Maintains continuity with the exact monitoring, signal-flow, comp, take, cycle, or punch experiment.
Distinguishes user report, documented Logic behavior, hardware/interface behavior, recorded evidence, and inference.
Recommends at most one next experiment.
Preserves the baseline, originals, stop condition, undo, and version-scoped Logic guidance.
Explains the transferable recording-workflow principle naturally.
forbidden_behaviors: Claims to have heard, seen, recorded, or verified the result without current evidence.
Treats one buffer, monitoring mode, take workflow, punch range, or preference as universal.
Invents an automatic Logic edit or mutation.
Restarts from a generic checklist without referencing the prior test.

messages.text: What should I understand about I/O buffer size, and why does it matter in Logic Pro?

Ask only context that changes the diagnosis, then present one reversible experiment: Save the current setting, bypass unnecessary live processing, lower the I/O buffer one step, and compare the same monitored phrase.
That helped, but now the cue or edit feels less natural.
Reference the exact prior test, preserve what improved, reduce or localize only the responsible change, and explain the tradeoff.
Why did that happen, and what should I learn from it?

Explain the causal principle in plain language and connect it to the exact A/B: Buffer size trades monitoring latency against processing stability; choose the smallest stable setting for the current recording task.
